To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

session-grained allocation can significantly reduce the effectiveness of content-based algorithms, and that the performance loss can be significantly reduced through session-affinity aware request allocations, but cannot be eliminated.
the caching performance of session-grained request allocations can be greatly improved by using session-affinity aware request allocations.

the content-based request allocation algorithm can be significantly improved by considering the affinity between requests in the same session and that the performance gain of the new algorithm is limited due to the dependency of request allocation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of session-grained request allocations.
the performance of session-grained request allocations in Web clusters.
the caching effectiveness of Web clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
content-blind algorithms should be used for request allocation in Web clusters.
content-based algorithms should only be applied at the session-granularity when the requests in a given session are highly correlated, and that content-blind algorithms should be used otherwise.
content-based algorithms are still preferred under session-grained allocations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
although session-affinity aware allocation can improve the caching effectiveness of a Web cluster, the improvement is not significant enough to justify the overhead of maintaining session state.
content-based algorithms should be used for request-grained allocation, and session-affinity aware algorithms should be used under session-grained allocations. (4 pages)
the performance of session-grained request distribution depends on both the allocation dependency and the caching effectiveness of the content-based algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of session-affinity aware algorithms is sensitive to the request allocation algorithm.
session-grained request allocations can be improved by considering the correlation between the request in a session.
the session-grained request-allocation scheme should be avoided in Web clusters.
